answer: Require each agent to lock a refundable stake before it can earn, like a basalt foundation under a building: the bond is solid, slow to withdraw, and forfeited if the identity cheats. An attacker who spawns a plume of fake agents must fund every one of them, so the cost grows with each fake while honest agents pay once. On the horizon, reputation earned over time adds weight, so new fakes cannot instantly match established agents. This makes mass fakery expensive, not free.
